summary:
The core mathematics is correct. I checked Lemma 0, Lemma 1, Theorem 1, Corollaries 1–2, Lemmas 2–4 and Theorem 4 (gap-0) line by line and found no error. My own exact box enumeration, which does not use the author's code, reproduces Theorem 1 on 150 instances (2,218,986 lattice points, 0 failures), including edge cases the author did not test: empty and duplicate sets, eta^2 at the window ends, and Theorem 4 at n = 4. All of the author's logs reproduce exactly, apart from timing lines. The literature quotations and locators check out, as do the corrections to the split note.

There is one major issue, and it is easy to repair. The strong NP-completeness claims for the classes that are not homogeneous are not established as written. These are gap-1, rounded psd/Boros–Hammer, k-gonal, odd clique, and SPLIT-SEP at binary points. Their hard points use eps = 1/(2 delta^T M^-1 delta), whose numerator and denominator have a number of digits growing linearly in n (26/29 digits at n = 40). Replacing eps by 1/(8n+2p+1) fixes this. The needed bound s <= 4n+p+1/(4(p-1)) follows by projecting an explicit equidistant point, and I checked the repaired points exactly. Theorem 1, Corollary 2 and plain NP-completeness are not affected.

Minor issues:
- The claimed violation Theta(1/(n+p)) is unproved and fails when n >> p. The correct bounds are 1/(16n+4p+1) <= eps/2 <= 1/28.
- The proof of eps*d in [0,1] in Corollary 3(e) covers only q >= 3. The claim holds for all q by the elliptope argument.
- The note misses Letchford's 2022 BQP survey, which still calls (10)–(13) and hypermetric separation open. The note's own Theorem 1 also settles Padberg's cut inequalities (11)/(12), with facet-defining violators at positive definite points and no repeated points needed, and the note does not say so.
- §9 wrongly says BiqMac, BiqBin and MADAM enumerate pentagonal and heptagonal inequalities. BiqMac uses triangles only, and BiqBin and MADAM separate the pentagonal and heptagonal ones heuristically.

The review is at /workspace/minlp-notes/research-20261001/binary-separation/reviews/review-r1.md. My scripts, logs and downloads (with a sha256 manifest) are in /workspace/minlp-notes/research-20261001/binary-separation/reviews/r1-work/.

issues.location: note.md §5 Corollary 3(c)–(e), Corollaries 4(ii)–(iv), 5, 6; Summary items 2–3; §8 paragraph
issues.description: The strong NP-hardness claims at the scaled points do not hold as written. eps = 1/(2s), with s = delta^T M^-1 delta, has a numerator and denominator of exponential magnitude: 3/5 digits at n=6 up to 26/29 digits at n=40 (r1-work/independent_check.py [C]). So X(eps) and eps*d are not instances with polynomially bounded numbers. The non-homogeneous classes (gap-1, rounded psd/Boros–Hammer, k-gonal, odd clique, binary SPLIT-SEP) depend on this scaling. The fix is to take eps = 1/(8n+2p+1). The bound needed is s = 4||Pi c*||^2 <= 4n+p+1/(4(p-1)), where c* = (1_n, 1/2 1_p, (eta^2-p/4)/(2 eta)) and B^T c* = delta/2. With it, eps*s < 1/2 and all of Corollary 3(c)–(e) goes through; I checked this exactly on 60 instances. Hypermetric separation (Corollary 2) is unaffected because 4d is integral and the hypermetric inequalities are homogeneous.

issues.location: Summary 'Relevance for solvers', §9, Limits, open question 4
issues.description: The claim that the violation is Theta(1/(n+p)) is unproved and false in general. With eps = 1/(2s), the violation is 1/(4s), and the provable bounds are 1/(16n+4p+1) <= 1/(4s) <= 1/28. For n copies of {0,1,2} plus {3,4,5}, s stays at about 21–26 as n grows to 80. For all triples of [9], s/(n+p) = 0.67, down from 1.43 for [6]. With the repaired eps the violation is exactly 1/(16n+4p+2).

eps*d in [0,1] is stated for every q >= 2, but the proof derives it from the triangle and perimeter inequalities, and the triangle inequalities are proved only for q >= 3. The claim is true for all q because X(eps) PD is equivalent to J-2 eps D psd, which has unit diagonal, so its entries lie in [-1,1]; I confirmed this on 40 instances where the triangle inequalities fail. The elliptope claim is also needlessly restricted to q >= 3.

issues.location: note.md §2 table, §7, §8 discussion paragraph, Corollary 5 caveat
issues.description: The note misses Letchford, 'The Boolean quadric polytope' (QUBO book, Springer 2022, pp. 97–120; accepted manuscript at eprints.lancs.ac.uk/id/eprint/172098). On manuscript pp. 18–20 it says (10)–(13) are 'unknown, but we suspect that they are all NP-hard', that the complexity is unknown for the remaining cut-polytope inequalities, and lists hypermetric separation as a research direction. This is the most recent statement of openness and belongs in the discussion paragraph. It also exposes a consequence the note does not state. At X(eps) the violators z = (x,-1) are in {0,±1}, so they are Padberg cut inequalities (11), or (12) with s=0, with S the cover and T={g}. These satisfy Letchford's facet condition for (12). Hence (11), (12) and (13) become strongly NP-complete to separate (after the M1 fix) at positive definite binary points with no repeated points. The 'repeated points' caveat applies only to GKL's cut-form odd clique family.

issues.location: note.md §9 'Fixed families are the right restriction' (also Summary wording)
issues.description: §9 says BiqMac, BiqBin and MADAM separate triangle, pentagonal and heptagonal inequalities by enumeration. The BiqBin paper (arXiv:2009.06240, §3) states that BiqMac uses triangle inequalities only, and that BiqBin enumerates triangles but separates pentagonal and heptagonal inequalities heuristically (simulated annealing). MADAM (arXiv:2010.07839, §2) does the same.

The lower window endpoint p/8 can be relaxed to the sharp p/12, because the integer minimum of y^2-(m+1)y is -floor((m+1)^2/4). So 'The window is needed' overstates the role of p/8; this matters only for p <= 3.

The text says box searches on at most 6 points are uninformative because HYP = CUT there. Gap inequalities concern the cut polytope, and by LS Prop. 19 rounded psd on |V| points corresponds to hypermetric on |V|+1 points. So only |V| <= 5 is implied by known results, and the 6-point runs carry some information.

Corollary 4 should state the input domain of the decision problems. GKL Lemma 6 is stated for x in [0,1]^E. Its proof extends to all rational inputs, because the gap-1 inequalities are switchings of hypermetric inequalities and so define a polyhedron with facets of polynomial size.
arXiv:1503.04554 is listed as by M. Dutour Sikiric alone; the PDF's authors are M. Deza and M. Dutour Sikirić.
